Common Methods: Correlation, regression, ANOVA, clustering, PCA, ML classification
Intuitive Analysis Logic: “What is happening right now?” Analyze associations, group differences, correlations, and patterns. No temporal causality.
Main Goal: Understand relationships at one time point

Common Methods: Survival analysis, mixed models, longitudinal regression
Intuitive Analysis Logic: “Who develops the outcome later?” Time matters. Baseline variables predict future events.
“What factors may explain the outcome?” Look backward from outcome to exposures.
Main Goal: Compare people with vs without an outcome

Intuitive Analysis Logic: “Did the intervention cause change?” Randomization reduces bias and improves causal confidence.
Similar to RCT but weaker causal confidence because groups may differ initially.
“How do individuals evolve?” Dependency between repeated measurements becomes important.
Mostly descriptive and exploratory. Focus on prevalence and distributions.
Clinical or exploratory insight rather than statistical inference.
“How accurately can this tool detect disease?” Focus is prediction accuracy against gold standard.
Prediction matters more than explanation. Generalization and validation are critical.

Common Methods: Random Forest, XGBoost, deep learning, feature selection
Intuitive Analysis Logic: Focus shifts from inference to robustness, validation, overfitting, feature engineering, and reproducibility.
Interpretation replaces numerical inference. Themes and concepts are extracted from text.
Use numbers for patterns and interviews for interpretation and context.
Literature itself becomes the dataset. Bias assessment becomes central.
Pool effect sizes across papers to estimate overall effect.
